speciesSyntax: formula[^charge][(phase)]; hν = photon; M = third body

reactions.name: Combustion of methane
reactions.description: Complete combustion of natural gas. Liquid water is the conventional product for the standard enthalpy of combustion (higher heating value).
caveats: Real flames proceed through hundreds of radical elementary steps (e.g. GRI-Mech 3.0).
reactions.citation: OpenStax Chemistry 2e (Flowers, Theopold, Langley & Robinson, 2019; CC BY 4.0), §5.3

reactions.name: Combustion of hydrogen
reactions.description: Formation of water from its elements; twice the standard enthalpy of formation of liquid water.
reactions.citation: OpenStax Chemistry 2e (Flowers, Theopold, Langley & Robinson, 2019; CC BY 4.0), §5.3

reactions.name: Combustion of hydrogen (water vapour product)
reactions.description: Same stoichiometry with gaseous water (lower heating value). Comparing with the liquid-water version isolates the enthalpy of vaporisation (Hess’s law).
reactions.citation: OpenStax Chemistry 2e (Flowers, Theopold, Langley & Robinson, 2019; CC BY 4.0), §5.3

reactions.name: Combustion of ethanol
reactions.description: Complete combustion of liquid ethanol (biofuel).
reactions.citation: OpenStax Chemistry 2e (Flowers, Theopold, Langley & Robinson, 2019; CC BY 4.0), §5.3

reactions.name: Combustion of propane
reactions.description: Complete combustion of propane (LPG).
reactions.citation: OpenStax Chemistry 2e (Flowers, Theopold, Langley & Robinson, 2019; CC BY 4.0), §4.1

reactions.name: Combustion of ethane
reactions.description: Complete combustion of ethane.
reactions.citation: OpenStax Chemistry 2e (Flowers, Theopold, Langley & Robinson, 2019; CC BY 4.0), §4.1

reactions.name: Combustion of n-octane
reactions.description: Idealised gasoline combustion (gasoline is a mixture; n-octane is a model compound).
reactions.citation: OpenStax Chemistry 2e (Flowers, Theopold, Langley & Robinson, 2019; CC BY 4.0), §4.1

reactions.name: Combustion of methanol
reactions.description: Complete combustion of liquid methanol.
reactions.citation: OpenStax Chemistry 2e (Flowers, Theopold, Langley & Robinson, 2019; CC BY 4.0), §4.1

reactions.name: Combustion of acetylene
reactions.description: Oxy-acetylene welding flame chemistry (net).
reactions.citation: OpenStax Chemistry 2e (Flowers, Theopold, Langley & Robinson, 2019; CC BY 4.0), §4.1

reactions.name: Combustion of carbon (graphite)
reactions.description: Formation reaction of CO₂ from its elements in their reference states.
reactions.citation: OpenStax Chemistry 2e (Flowers, Theopold, Langley & Robinson, 2019; CC BY 4.0), §5.3

reactions.name: Oxidation of carbon monoxide
reactions.description: Burning of CO (the second step of a Hess cycle C → CO → CO₂); also the main reaction in automotive catalytic converters.
reactions.citation: OpenStax Chemistry 2e (Flowers, Theopold, Langley & Robinson, 2019; CC BY 4.0), §5.3

reactions.name: Partial oxidation of carbon
reactions.description: Formation of CO; cannot be measured cleanly by calorimetry (some CO₂ always forms), so its enthalpy is classically obtained by Hess’s law.
reactions.citation: OpenStax Chemistry 2e (Flowers, Theopold, Langley & Robinson, 2019; CC BY 4.0), §5.3

reactions.name: Haber–Bosch ammonia synthesis
reactions.description: Fixation of atmospheric nitrogen; exothermic with a decrease in gas moles, so equilibrium favours ammonia at low T and high p while kinetics needs high T.
reactions.citation: Greenwood & Earnshaw, Chemistry of the Elements, 2nd ed. (Butterworth-Heinemann, 1997), ch. 11

reactions.name: Contact process: oxidation of SO₂
reactions.description: Key step of sulfuric-acid manufacture.
reactions.citation: Greenwood & Earnshaw, Chemistry of the Elements, 2nd ed. (Butterworth-Heinemann, 1997), ch. 15

reactions.name: Hydration of SO₃ to sulfuric acid
reactions.description: Net result of the contact process (industrially SO₃ is absorbed in H₂SO₄ to form oleum, then diluted). In the atmosphere the same net change produces sulfate aerosol and acid rain.
reactions.citation: Greenwood & Earnshaw, Chemistry of the Elements, 2nd ed. (Butterworth-Heinemann, 1997), ch. 15

reactions.name: Ostwald process: catalytic oxidation of ammonia
reactions.description: First step of nitric-acid manufacture.
reactions.citation: Greenwood & Earnshaw, Chemistry of the Elements, 2nd ed. (Butterworth-Heinemann, 1997), ch. 11

reactions.name: Steam–methane reforming
reactions.description: Main industrial source of hydrogen; strongly endothermic.
reactions.citation: Greenwood & Earnshaw, Chemistry of the Elements, 2nd ed. (Butterworth-Heinemann, 1997), ch. 3

reactions.name: Water–gas shift
reactions.description: Converts CO to additional H₂ after reforming; mildly exothermic.
reactions.citation: Greenwood & Earnshaw, Chemistry of the Elements, 2nd ed. (Butterworth-Heinemann, 1997), ch. 3

reactions.name: Methanol synthesis
reactions.description: Synthesis-gas route to methanol.
reactions.citation: Greenwood & Earnshaw, Chemistry of the Elements, 2nd ed. (Butterworth-Heinemann, 1997), ch. 8

reactions.name: Calcination of limestone
reactions.description: Lime production; a major industrial CO₂ source independent of fuel combustion.
reactions.citation: Greenwood & Earnshaw, Chemistry of the Elements, 2nd ed. (Butterworth-Heinemann, 1997), ch. 5

reactions.name: Electrolysis of water
reactions.description: Reverse of hydrogen combustion, driven by electrical work (ΔG° = +237 kJ per mol H₂O must be supplied).
reactions.citation: OpenStax Chemistry 2e (Flowers, Theopold, Langley & Robinson, 2019; CC BY 4.0), §17.7

reactions.name: Neutralisation of HCl by NaOH (molecular equation)
reactions.description: Strong acid + strong base. In solution all species except water are ions; see the net ionic form.
reactions.citation: OpenStax Chemistry 2e (Flowers, Theopold, Langley & Robinson, 2019; CC BY 4.0), §4.2

reactions.name: Neutralisation (net ionic equation)
reactions.description: The only chemical change in any strong acid–strong base neutralisation; H⁺(aq) stands for the hydrated proton (H₃O⁺ and larger clusters).
reactions.citation: OpenStax Chemistry 2e (Flowers, Theopold, Langley & Robinson, 2019; CC BY 4.0), §4.2

reactions.name: Ammonia as a Brønsted base
reactions.description: Weak-base equilibrium (K_b ≈ 1.8 × 10⁻⁵ at 25 °C, OpenStax Appendix I).
reactions.citation: OpenStax Chemistry 2e (Flowers, Theopold, Langley & Robinson, 2019; CC BY 4.0), §14.3

reactions.name: Dissociation of acetic acid
reactions.description: Weak-acid equilibrium (K_a ≈ 1.8 × 10⁻⁵ at 25 °C, OpenStax Appendix H).
reactions.citation: OpenStax Chemistry 2e (Flowers, Theopold, Langley & Robinson, 2019; CC BY 4.0), §14.3

reactions.name: Dissolved CO₂ ⇌ bicarbonate
reactions.description: Combines hydration of CO₂ to H₂CO₃ and its first dissociation. Governs ocean acidification and (via carbonic anhydrase) blood pH buffering.
reactions.citation: Zeebe & Wolf-Gladrow, CO₂ in Seawater: Equilibrium, Kinetics, Isotopes (Elsevier, 2001)

reactions.name: Precipitation of silver chloride
reactions.description: Classical chloride test (K_sp ≈ 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁰, OpenStax Appendix J).
reactions.citation: OpenStax Chemistry 2e (Flowers, Theopold, Langley & Robinson, 2019; CC BY 4.0), §15.1

reactions.name: Precipitation of barium sulfate
reactions.description: Gravimetric sulfate determination; BaSO₄ is also the X-ray contrast agent (high-Z barium attenuates X-rays).
reactions.citation: OpenStax Chemistry 2e (Flowers, Theopold, Langley & Robinson, 2019; CC BY 4.0), §15.1

reactions.name: Precipitation of calcium carbonate
reactions.description: Limescale, limestone and the shells/skeletons of many marine organisms.
reactions.citation: OpenStax Chemistry 2e (Flowers, Theopold, Langley & Robinson, 2019; CC BY 4.0), §15.1

reactions.name: Carbonation weathering of limestone
reactions.description: Dissolution of limestone by carbonic acid (karst caves); the reverse forms stalactites.
reactions.citation: Zeebe & Wolf-Gladrow, CO₂ in Seawater (Elsevier, 2001)

reactions.name: Zinc displaces copper (Daniell cell reaction)
reactions.description: Overall cell reaction of the Daniell cell; E°cell = +1.10 V (OpenStax Appendix L).
reactions.citation: OpenStax Chemistry 2e (Flowers, Theopold, Langley & Robinson, 2019; CC BY 4.0), §17.2

reactions.name: Permanganate oxidises iron(II)
reactions.description: Classic redox titration in acid solution. Atoms and charge (+17 on each side) must balance.
reactions.citation: OpenStax Chemistry 2e (Flowers, Theopold, Langley & Robinson, 2019; CC BY 4.0), §17.1

reactions.name: Oxidation of iron (idealised rusting)
reactions.description: Net formation of anhydrous Fe₂O₃. Real rust is hydrated and forms electrochemically through Fe²⁺ intermediates in the presence of water.
caveats: Corrosion is an electrochemical multi-step process.
reactions.citation: OpenStax Chemistry 2e (Flowers, Theopold, Langley & Robinson, 2019; CC BY 4.0), §17.6

reactions.name: Thermite reaction
reactions.description: Highly exothermic metal–oxide exchange (molten iron produced).
reactions.citation: Greenwood & Earnshaw, Chemistry of the Elements, 2nd ed. (Butterworth-Heinemann, 1997), ch. 7

reactions.name: Sodium + chlorine → sodium chloride
reactions.description: Formation of an ionic solid from its elements.
reactions.citation: OpenStax Chemistry 2e (Flowers, Theopold, Langley & Robinson, 2019; CC BY 4.0), §7.5

reactions.name: Chapman cycle 1: photolysis of O₂
reactions.description: Ultraviolet photons below ~242 nm dissociate O₂ in the stratosphere.
reactions.citation: Chapman, S. (1930) Mem. R. Meteorol. Soc. 3, 103 — oxygen-only stratospheric ozone cycle; Seinfeld & Pandis, Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics, 3rd ed. (Wiley, 2016), ch. 5

reactions.name: Chapman cycle 2: ozone formation
reactions.description: Three-body recombination; M carries away the excess energy so O₃ does not immediately fall apart.
reactions.citation: Chapman, S. (1930) Mem. R. Meteorol. Soc. 3, 103 — oxygen-only stratospheric ozone cycle; Seinfeld & Pandis, Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics, 3rd ed. (Wiley, 2016), ch. 5

reactions.name: Chapman cycle 3: photolysis of O₃
reactions.description: Ozone absorbs UV-B/UV-C (the Hartley band, peak ≈ 255 nm); this absorption is what shields the surface.
reactions.citation: Chapman, S. (1930) Mem. R. Meteorol. Soc. 3, 103 — oxygen-only stratospheric ozone cycle; Seinfeld & Pandis, Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics, 3rd ed. (Wiley, 2016), ch. 5

reactions.name: Chapman cycle 4: O + O₃
reactions.description: Odd-oxygen loss step of the Chapman mechanism.
reactions.citation: Chapman, S. (1930) Mem. R. Meteorol. Soc. 3, 103 — oxygen-only stratospheric ozone cycle; Seinfeld & Pandis, Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics, 3rd ed. (Wiley, 2016), ch. 5

reactions.name: Chlorine catalytic cycle step 1
reactions.description: Chlorine atoms from photolysed CFCs destroy ozone…
reactions.citation: Molina & Rowland (1974) Nature 249, 810 — chlorine-catalysed ozone destruction

reactions.name: Chlorine catalytic cycle step 2
reactions.description: …and are regenerated, so one Cl atom can remove many O₃ molecules (net: O + O₃ → 2 O₂).
reactions.citation: Molina & Rowland (1974) Nature 249, 810 — chlorine-catalysed ozone destruction

reactions.name: NO titration of ozone
reactions.description: Fast reaction that removes ozone near NO sources (traffic).
reactions.citation: Seinfeld & Pandis, Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics, 3rd ed. (Wiley, 2016), ch. 6

reactions.name: Photolysis of NO₂
reactions.description: The only significant tropospheric source of O atoms (and thus ground-level ozone via O + O₂ + M).
reactions.citation: Seinfeld & Pandis, Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics, 3rd ed. (Wiley, 2016), ch. 6

reactions.name: Methane + hydroxyl radical
reactions.description: Rate-limiting first step of atmospheric methane removal; sets methane’s ~9–12-year lifetime.
reactions.citation: Seinfeld & Pandis, Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics, 3rd ed. (Wiley, 2016), ch. 6

reactions.name: H₂ formation on dust grains
reactions.description: Gas-phase H + H cannot shed the binding energy fast enough; grain surfaces catalyse the most abundant molecule in the Universe.
caveats: The grain is a catalyst and is not written in the equation.
reactions.citation: Gould & Salpeter (1963) ApJ 138, 393; Hollenbach & Salpeter (1971) ApJ 163, 155

reactions.name: H₃⁺ formation
reactions.description: Fast ion–molecule reaction following cosmic-ray ionisation of H₂; H₃⁺ then drives most interstellar gas-phase chemistry.
reactions.citation: Tielens, A. G. G. M. (2013) Rev. Mod. Phys. 85, 1021 — the molecular universe

reactions.name: Radiative association of C⁺ with H₂
reactions.description: Slow but important route into hydrocarbon chemistry in diffuse clouds; the excess energy leaves as a photon.
reactions.citation: Tielens, A. G. G. M. (2013) Rev. Mod. Phys. 85, 1021 — the molecular universe

reactions.name: Oxygenic photosynthesis (net equation)
reactions.conditions: driven by absorbed visible light (≈ 400–700 nm) in chloroplasts
reactions.description: Net equation only. The real process comprises the light-dependent reactions (photosystems II and I, electron transport, ATP synthase) and the Calvin–Benson cycle; it consumes ≥ 8 photons per O₂.
caveats: Not an elementary reaction: dozens of enzymatic steps.
O₂ released comes from water, not CO₂ — the net equation hides this.
reactions.citation: Berg, Tymoczko, Gatto & Stryer, Biochemistry, 9th ed. (W. H. Freeman, 2019), ch. 19–20

reactions.name: Aerobic respiration of glucose (net equation)
reactions.description: Net equation of glycolysis + pyruvate oxidation + citric-acid cycle + oxidative phosphorylation. Chemically identical to burning glucose; in cells the free energy is captured as ~30–32 ATP per glucose.
caveats: Not an elementary reaction: > 20 enzymatic steps in two cellular compartments.
ATP yield per glucose is an estimate (P/O ratios), not a stoichiometric constant.
reactions.citation: Berg, Tymoczko, Gatto & Stryer, Biochemistry, 9th ed. (W. H. Freeman, 2019), ch. 16–18

reactions.name: Lactic-acid fermentation (net)
reactions.description: Anaerobic glycolysis in muscle and lactic-acid bacteria. At physiological pH the product is lactate⁻ + H⁺.
caveats: Net equation; the pathway has 11 enzymatic steps.
reactions.citation: Berg, Tymoczko, Gatto & Stryer, Biochemistry, 9th ed. (W. H. Freeman, 2019), ch. 16

reactions.name: Alcoholic fermentation (net)
reactions.description: Yeast metabolism under anaerobic conditions.
caveats: Net equation; glycolysis plus pyruvate decarboxylation and reduction.
reactions.citation: Berg, Tymoczko, Gatto & Stryer, Biochemistry, 9th ed. (W. H. Freeman, 2019), ch. 16

reactions.name: ATP hydrolysis (neutral-species bookkeeping)
reactions.description: Atom bookkeeping for ATP + H₂O → ADP + Pᵢ. In cells these species are mostly ionised and Mg²⁺-bound; the biologically relevant free energy depends on pH, [Mg²⁺] and concentrations.
caveats: Standard-state thermochemistry of the neutral species is not the cellular ΔG.
reactions.citation: Berg, Tymoczko, Gatto & Stryer, Biochemistry, 9th ed. (W. H. Freeman, 2019), ch. 15
